chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: He narrated to me Al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The roots of infidelity are three: greed, haughtiness, and jealousy. As for greed, it was Adam when he was forbidden from the tree; greed compelled him to eat from it. As for haughtiness, it was Satan when he was ordered to prostrate, but he refused. As for jealousy, it was the two sons of Adam when one killed the other out of jealousy.
ai.seo_question: What are the three roots of infidelity according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifying greed, haughtiness, and jealousy as the three foundational roots of infidelity, linking them to the primordial narratives of Adam, Iblis, and Qabil. This triad illustrates how internal spiritual defects manifest as the primary causes of deviation, establishing a psychological framework for understanding the fall from divine proximity. The narration serves as a key hermeneutical tool in Shia theology for diagnosing the spiritual ailments that lead to *kufr* beyond mere denial of God.
